summary: LimeSuiteNG 37cb183 with the TX-rejecting patch of the TX audit parts 1 and 2 (recipes/limesuiteng/TX-AUDIT.md, AUDIT_DRAFT_CI_CHECKED): core library, SoapySDR module and headers; LimeSDR-Micro the only board; no CLI, GUI, GNU Radio, Amarisoft, firmware, udev, kernel modules, USB (FX3/FT601) or LimePCIe (X3/XTRX/MMX8/sSDR) boards

notes: Options of deployment/build-vendor.sh limesuiteng kept (BUILD_GUI/CLI/DOCS/UNIT_TESTS/AMARISOFT/GNURADIO/HDSDR=OFF, SOAPYSDR=ON, UDEV/FIRMWARE install OFF); every other option the pinned tree declares is set to its upstream default.

Four deliberate non-defaults: BUILD_DRIVERS=OFF (la9310_limesdr 0.2.1 and la9310_uart_module 1.0.0 are their own DKMS components in sources.lock.json and need linux-headers-6.18.2-4-qcom, not this chroot); BUILD_LEGACYAPI=OFF (build/07 section 10: only when a consumer needs it); RPATH automation OFF as in the upstream debian/rules, so no RPATH enters a system library; LIMESUITENG_USB_FX3/FTDI=OFF (TX audit part 1, recipes/limesuiteng/TX-AUDIT.md E-04).

LIMESUITENG_USB_FX3/FTDI=OFF removes the LimeSDR-USB and LimeSDR-Mini board drivers (src/boards/CMakeLists.txt:15-23 at 37cb183), whose own TX paths are not patched and which are not part of this device; LIMESUITENG_PCIE stays ON because LimeSDR_Micro is built under it (src/boards/CMakeLists.txt:6-13).

TX audit part 2: the patch also removes the LimePCIe boards LimeSDR-X3, LimeSDR-XTRX, MMX8 and sSDR and DeviceFactoryPCIe from the build (src/boards/CMakeLists.txt:7-12, src/boards/BoardSupportLoader.in.cpp:24 at 37cb183), so LimeSDR_Micro is the only board and TRXLooper has no constructing board; the first forbid_strings check proves their typeinfo names are gone from the library. LA9310_TRX::Setup rejects TX channels and its Transmit returns 0.

The second forbid_strings check: the SoapySDR module, the only consumer of the library, references no symbol or type of the raw-access classes (LMS7002M, LimeSDR_Micro, MCU_BD, LA9310*, VSPA*, PHYTimer*, LimePCIe, the other chips, GetRegister, LimePlugin); it reaches the device only through the guarded SDRDevice virtual methods (TX-AUDIT.md section L).

deploy.py verify_build still rejects every Lime runtime library until the complete native/raw-register TX audit (sources.lock.json release_blockers) is REVIEWED; this build proves only that the patched tree compiles and packages on arm64.
